decision: Running on the MacBook for now: no hardware to buy. The Raspberry Pi build below is optional and can be revisited later.
note: Prices are as listed by the sources on the date shown and will vary. Nothing here has been purchased or hardware-tested by Claude.

primary_setup.display: MacBook screen, recipe app open at https://devinberens.github.io
primary_setup.microphone: MacBook built-in mic, or the USB mic already owned (set AUDIO_INPUT_DEVICE)
primary_setup.speaker: MacBook speakers or headphones

need.item: Raspberry Pi 5 (+ case, active cooler, USB-C power supply)

options.name: Hosyond 10.1-inch IPS capacitive touchscreen (Amazon ASIN B0BHQRSDZR)
options.why: Cheapest 10-inch option, 1024x600 IPS, tempered-glass touch, built-in dual speakers, and the listing title names Raspberry Pi 5/4/3. Power it from its own wall adapter; confirm a micro-HDMI cable or adapter is in the box for the Pi 5.

options.name: Wimaxit M1012 10.1-inch touchscreen (B&H)
options.why: Backup: 1024x600, 5-point touch, built-in speakers, includes HDMI to micro-HDMI adapter; listed for Pi 2/3/4 only

options.name: UPERFECT OD101BF 10-inch touchscreen
options.why: 10-inch Full HD (1920x1200) touchscreen built for Raspberry Pi

need.size_note: 15.6-inch models ruled out as too big for the counter; staying at about 10 inches.

need.item: Speaker (optional: try the monitor's built-in speakers first)

software.text_to_speech: macOS 'say' (default on Mac); Piper on Linux/Pi
